qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Sub-hurdle capital efficiency with 5-year median GAAP ROIC of only 7.45%, well below the 12% hurdle. While Dupixent is a commercial success in immunology, historical legacy acquisitions have bloated the asset base (goodwill and intangibles of €67.6B), and upcoming 2031 Dupixent patent expiration creates severe concentration risk without adequate organic R&D return proof.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (N, REJECT). Sanofi fails the empirical proof-of-moat test with a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of only 7.45% (hurdle >= 12%), burdened by €67.6B in capitalized intangibles/goodwill from dilutive historical M&A and facing severe concentration risk ahead of Dupixent's 2031 patent cliff.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 7.45% (FY2022: 10.9%, FY2023: 7.4%, FY2024: 7.5%, FY2025: 7.1%), failing the 12% hurdle. Intangibles and goodwill total €67.6B against €71.4B in equity, reflecting massive historical capital deployment that fails to generate super-normal economic returns.
